title: The Building With No Plaque
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] The board voted unanimously to name the clinic after me, a gesture I understood was meant warmly, and which I nonetheless spent a restless week trying to politely dismantle.
Narrator: I had funded most of its construction, true enough, but funding a thing and owning its meaning felt, to me, like two claims that shouldn't automatically travel together.

Narrator: [carefully] The chair seemed genuinely baffled by my resistance, pointing out, not unreasonably, that plaques exist precisely to encourage future donors by demonstrating that generosity gets remembered.
Narrator: I couldn't entirely dismiss that argument, since visible philanthropy does, empirically, seem to invite more of itself, a pragmatic case I found harder to refute than I expected.
Narrator: [reflective] Still, I noticed something uncomfortable in how quickly I'd begun rehearsing modest responses to a compliment nobody had even offered yet.
Narrator: That rehearsal alone told me something, that some quiet corner of me had already begun composing the gracious speech I'd give while accepting recognition I claimed not to want.

Narrator: [honestly] So I proposed a compromise instead, funding continues, my name stays entirely off any signage, but I'll personally thank donors who do want recognition, redirecting the visibility elsewhere.
Narrator: The board accepted, somewhat reluctantly, and the clinic now bears the name of the neighborhood it serves, which strikes me as considerably more accurate anyway.
Narrator: [gently] Patients walking in now have no idea who financed their care, which is, I've decided, precisely the correct amount of information for them to carry.

Narrator: I still visit occasionally, unannounced, standing in the waiting room like any other stranger, and there's a particular satisfaction in that anonymity I doubt a plaque could have ever replicated.
Narrator: [calmly] Perhaps I'll change my mind eventually, considering the board's pragmatic argument again with age, but for now the nameless building feels like the truer monument.
